final.title: The real limit of a knowledge assistant
final.body:
A knowledge assistant has a simple limit: it is only useful when the answer lives in approved company documents. For a small-business owner, that makes it a workflow decision, not a buzzword decision. If the question can be answered from your own policies, FAQs, product notes, or other text you already control, a grounded assistant may fit. If it needs open-web research, judgment calls, or human approval, it is probably the wrong tool for that job.

That is the practical filter I would use before comparing manual work, hiring, or a bounded automation investment. Bareni’s self-built demo shows the mechanics only: it can ingest MD, PDF, and URL content, run vector search and reranking, generate grounded answers, and show sources. It is a local demo on synthetic Acme Shop data, and it does not prove production use, customer validation, billing, rate limiting, or scale.

So the next step is straightforward: pick one recurring workflow and ask, “Could my team answer this by looking in our own documents, or do they need to research outside?” If the honest answer is outside research, keep it human. If it is inside your documents, that is the workflow worth testing.
